title: Backup export/import omits profile, goals, and display prefs
description: exportAllDataAsJSON() (index.html, function starting ~line 1562) only writes state.logEntries and state.customFoods into the backup payload. It does not include state.profile, state.goals, or state.displayPrefs, even though these are all persisted separately in localStorage (STORAGE_PROFILE = "nt_profile", STORAGE_GOALS = "nt_goals", STORAGE_DISPLAY_PREFS = "nt_displayPrefs", declared at lines 556-558) and represent real user-facing features: the onboarding profile (weight/height/age/sex/activity/goal used by calculateGoals()) and the Settings screen's per-nutrient goal overrides and 'show on totals card' display toggles. The matching import handler (the importFile 'change' listener, ~line 1622) only reads data.logEntries and data.customFoods back out, so it can't restore these fields even if they were present. A code comment directly above exportAllDataAsJSON() (~line 1567-1569) says 'there's no settings-backed state anywhere in this app yet (only nt_customFoods and nt_logEntries exist in localStorage)' -- this is now stale/incorrect since nt_profile, nt_goals, and nt_displayPrefs were added in a later feature pass and the export/import code was never updated to match. Net effect: a user who downloads a backup and restores it on a new device (or after clearing site data) silently loses their onboarding profile and any custom goal/display-preference customizations, while food log and custom foods survive intact.
fixNotes: exportAllDataAsJSON() now emits a v2.0 payload including profile, goals, and displayPrefs (nested log.logEntries/log.customFoods, top-level preferences) alongside the food log, the stale settings-backed-state comment was removed, and the importFile change handler now detects v2.0 vs. legacy flat v1.0 backups and restores profile/goals/preferences (when present) via saveProfile()/saveGoals()/saveDisplayPrefs() in addition to the existing customFoods/logEntries restore.

title: foods.json: 20 items missing required 'category' field
description: The first 20 entries in foods.json (the original generic food set, ids: chicken-breast, brown-rice, egg, greek-yogurt, banana, apple, almonds, peanut-butter, oatmeal, salmon, broccoli, sweet-potato, whole-milk, white-bread, avocado, ground-beef, black-beans, cheddar-cheese, spinach, orange-juice) have no 'category' field, while all 48 items added afterward (the Kirkland/branded set, ids starting at 'kirkland-smoked-salmon' onward) do include one (e.g. "category": "protein", "fruit", "beverage", etc). This is schema drift introduced when the food list grew from 20 to 68 items across several separate additions -- the newer entries adopted a field the original set never had. Currently low-impact since index.html's JS never reads a food item's .category (renderFoodList() only uses f.name, f.brand, f.servingSize, f.servingUnit, f.calories, f.custom -- grep confirms the only '.category' usage in the whole file is for vitamins.json grouping, not foods.json), so nothing breaks today. But it violates the qa-reviewer data-integrity checklist requirement that every food item have an id/name/category/calories/macros, and any future feature that groups or filters the food list by category (a natural extension given vitamins.json already supports it) would silently misbehave for these 20 items.
fixNotes: Added a 'category' field to all 20 generic-set foods.json entries (chicken-breast, brown-rice, egg, greek-yogurt, banana, apple, almonds, peanut-butter, oatmeal, salmon, broccoli, sweet-potato, whole-milk, white-bread, avocado, ground-beef, black-beans, cheddar-cheese, spinach, orange-juice), assigning values consistent with how the existing 48 branded items use the enum (e.g. fat-dominant items like almonds/avocado/peanut-butter categorized 'fat' like the Kirkland nut butters and oils, legumes categorized 'vegetable' like kirkland-frozen-edamame).

title: addLogEntry() never snapshots micronutrient fields onto log entries
description: During integration testing of the new micronutrient tracking feature (getDailyMicronutrientTotals/getMicronutrientStatus, index.html ~line 1060-1162, reading MICRONUTRIENT_KEYS off each food log entry), discovered that addLogEntry() (~line 1636-1648, pre-existing, unmodified by the feature work) only copies the 7 core NUTRIENT_KEYS (calories, protein_g, carbs_g, fat_g, sugar_g, fiber_g, sodium_mg) from the source food item onto the new log entry -- it never copies any of the 30 MICRONUTRIENT_KEYS fields (vitaminc_mg, iron_mg, omega3_mg, etc.). Since getDailyMicronutrientTotals() reads these fields directly off each day's log entries (not by re-looking-up the original food item), every micronutrient except sodium_mg (which happens to double as both a core NUTRIENT_KEY and a tracked micronutrient) silently totaled to zero/absent for every logged food, regardless of how much real data that food item actually had in foods.json. Caught by live testing: logged Kirkland Smoked Salmon (omega3_mg: 1000 in foods.json) and it showed 'Not logged today' in the micronutrient detail view, while Sodium correctly showed real totals from the same entries.
foundBy: claude (live integration testing after log-engine/ui-builder both reported success)
fixNotes: addLogEntry() now also copies any MICRONUTRIENT_KEYS field the source food item actually has data for onto the log entry (food[k] != null check, matching the sparse-field convention getDailyMicronutrientTotals() already expects -- fields the food doesn't track are left absent, not defaulted to 0). Verified live: freshly logging Kirkland Avocado Oil after the fix correctly showed Vitamin E 1.8/15mg (12%) in the micronutrient detail view.

title: Magnesium UL applied to food sources — should be supplements only
description: getMicronutrientStatus() applies the 350mg upper limit to all magnesium totals regardless of source. rdas.json line 271 explicitly notes the UL applies to supplemental magnesium only — dietary magnesium from food has no upper limit. Users eating normal amounts of nuts, greens, or whole grains easily exceed 350mg from food alone and get a false over_ul warning. Will get worse once supplement wiring lands since supplement magnesium will stack onto the same unqualified total.
fixNotes: Added isSupplementOnlyUL() helper. Magnesium UL check now skipped in getMicronutrientStatus() since current totals are food-only. TODO comment added for supplement wiring phase. FULL FIX LANDED (2026-08-10, via bug_005 + food/supplement breakdown feature): getMicronutrientStatus() now checks isSupplementOnlyUL()-flagged nutrients (magnesium, niacin, folate, vitamin E) against getDailySupplementMicronutrientTotals() specifically, not the combined food+supplement total -- the UL is no longer skipped, it's correctly scoped to supplement-sourced intake only.

title: Supplement log entries never contribute to micronutrient totals
description: Reported by user: logging a supplement (e.g. Zinc 50mg) does not update Today's Micronutrients -- the nutrient still shows as 'Not logged today'. Root cause: getDailyMicronutrientTotals() (index.html ~line 1111-1123) explicitly skips every log entry with type === "supplement" (line 1115), and even if it didn't, vitamins.json entries have no field mapping a supplement to a specific rdas.json nutrient key -- each entry only has a single headline amountPerDose/amountUnit (e.g. "Zinc 50mg") with nothing structurally linking it to zinc_mg, and no unit conversion (e.g. IU-to-mcg for Vitamin D3) exists either. logSupplement() (~line 1702) also never snapshots any nutrient contribution onto the log entry, unlike addLogEntry() for food (fixed in bug_003). This is a known, previously-documented gap (see CLAUDE.md Known Gaps and the qa-reviewer micronutrient audit, Check 4) now confirmed as user-facing. Also affects the magnesium UL fix from bug_004: isSupplementOnlyUL()-flagged nutrients (magnesium, niacin, folate, vitamin E) currently skip their upper-limit check entirely, since there is no supplement-sourced total to check against -- once supplement contributions are wired in, that check needs to run against the supplement-sourced portion specifically, not just be skipped.
affectedLines: index.html ~1111-1123 (getDailyMicronutrientTotals()), ~1702-1734 (logSupplement()), ~1161-1220 (getMicronutrientStatus(), isSupplementOnlyUL() gate from bug_004); vitamins.json (all 20 entries, missing nutrientKey/conversionFactor fields)
fixNotes: logSupplement() now snapshots entry.multiplier (dose/commonDose) and entry[vitamin.nutrientKey] (amountPerDose * conversionFactor) onto each supplement log entry, mirroring addLogEntry()'s food snapshot pattern; getDailyMicronutrientTotals() no longer skips type==="supplement" entries so they flow through the same MICRONUTRIENT_KEYS summation loop as food; added getDailySupplementMicronutrientTotals() to sum only supplement-sourced contributions; and getMicronutrientStatus() now checks the upper limit for supplement-only-UL nutrients (magnesium, niacin, folate, vitamin E) against that supplement-only total instead of skipping the check entirely, while all other nutrients keep checking the combined food+supplement total.

title: Micronutrient contributor toggle below touch target minimum
description: In the new micronutrient detail view (#microView), each micronutrient row can be expanded via a <details>/<summary> element to show which foods/supplements contributed to that nutrient total (microRowHtml(), index.html line 1655-1724). The .micro-contributors-toggle summary element (CSS line 372-376) uses min-height: 32px with padding: 4px 0, resulting in an effective touch target height of 40px (32 + 4 + 4). This falls short of the app established touch target standard of 44px, used throughout for interactive elements (button.remove-btn min-height: 44px line 141, .check-row min-height: 44px line 180, .cal-nav-btn width/height: 44px lines 255-256, etc.). On mobile devices (iPhone SE 375px, iPhone 14 390px), users may experience difficulty reliably tapping the toggle to expand/collapse the contributor list.
fixNotes: .micro-contributors-toggle min-height changed from 32px to 44px, matching the app-wide touch-target convention already used by .remove-btn/.check-row/.cal-nav-btn.

title: Contributor item names may overflow on narrow viewports
description: In the expanded micronutrient contributor list (microRowHtml() contributor rendering, index.html line 1692-1700), each item is a flex row (.micro-contributor-item, CSS line 380-383) with layout: display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: baseline; gap: 10px. The first child (a span containing icon + food/supplement name + brand) has NO flex: 1; min-width: 0 CSS properties. Without min-width: 0, the flex item won not shrink below its content natural width, preventing text wrapping when space-between pushes the amount (second span) to the right. Risk: on narrow viewports (iPhone SE 375px, iPhone 14 390px), if a food name is long, the name span will overflow horizontally instead of wrapping, breaking the layout. Comparison: .log-entry-info (similar flex space-between layout, line 129-131) correctly uses flex: 1; min-width: 0 to enable text wrapping.
fixNotes: Gave the contributor name span its own .micro-contributor-name class (flex: 1; min-width: 0; overflow-wrap: break-word) and the amount span .micro-contributor-amount (flex: 0 0 auto; white-space: nowrap), matching the .log-entry-info flex:1/min-width:0 pattern already used elsewhere for the same space-between-with-long-text layout. Long names now wrap instead of overflowing; the amount stays fixed on the right.

title: Camera stream leak on rapid barcode-scan cancel
description: stopBarcodeScanner() guarded on both html5QrcodeInstance AND barcodeScannerRunning being truthy before calling instance.stop(). html5QrcodeInstance is assigned synchronously right after Html5Qrcode construction, before start() is even invoked, but barcodeScannerRunning only flips true inside start()'s .then() once the promise resolves. In the window between construction and that resolution (camera permission prompt / device init), an instance exists but barcodeScannerRunning is still false -- if the user tapped Cancel fast enough during that window, stopBarcodeScanner() hit the early-return branch and never called instance.stop(), leaking the camera stream in the background (battery drain, camera indicator staying lit, privacy concern). Caught by qa-reviewer targeted audit of the new barcode-scanning feature.
fixNotes: Changed the guard to check html5QrcodeInstance alone, not also barcodeScannerRunning -- Html5Qrcode.stop() is already safe to call on a not-yet-fully-started instance (the existing .catch() covers "already stopped / never fully started"), so calling it unconditionally whenever an instance object exists is correct and has no downside.

title: Barcode scan buttons below 44px touch target convention
description: #scanBarcodeBtn and #barcodeModalCancel used the shared button.secondary class (padding:12px, no explicit min-height), landing a bit short of this app's established 44px touch-target convention already used by .remove-btn/.check-row/.cal-nav-btn/.micro-contributors-toggle/etc. Caught by qa-reviewer targeted audit of the new barcode-scanning feature.
fixNotes: Added min-height:44px scoped to #scanBarcodeBtn and #barcodeModalCancel specifically, rather than widening the shared button.secondary class everywhere it's already used across the app.

title: Log-modal default unit/amount looked like it meant hundreds of servings
description: The log-a-food modal's default ("native") unit option was labeled with the food's raw servingSize + servingUnit (e.g. "240 ml (1 cup)" for Kirkland 1% milk), and the Amount field defaulted to that same raw number (240). Visually this read as "Amount: 240, Unit: 240 ml (1 cup)" -- indistinguishable at a glance from logging 240 cups, even though the underlying math (multiplier = amount / food.servingSize) was correct and always produced exactly 1 serving by default. User reported this directly with a screenshot of the milk case and correctly identified it as confusing/risky: someone "fixing" it by typing 1 while leaving the unit unchanged would have actually logged only 1ml, a real silent under-log.
affectedLines: index.html: getAvailableLogUnits(), convertLogQuantityToMultiplier() native case, openLogModal(), modalUnitSelect change handler
fixNotes: Redesigned so the native/default unit option always means "number of servings" instead of "raw quantity in the food's own unit": label changed to a plain "servings" for every food (was food.servingSize + food.servingUnit), convertLogQuantityToMultiplier()'s native case changed from amount/food.servingSize to amount directly (no division), and the Amount field now defaults to 1 (was food.servingSize) both on modal open and when switching back to the native unit. The default "open modal, tap Log it" interaction is mathematically identical before and after (multiplier 1) -- verified across all 79 foods.json entries via 10 executable tests, not just reasoned about. Non-native unit paths (g/oz/lb/cup/tbsp/tsp/ml/fl-oz) were untouched. qa-reviewer independent audit: no findings. Live-tested on the exact milk case from the user's screenshot plus a 2-cup food (spinach) -- both now show Amount:1/Unit:servings and log the correct kcal.
